subject: Proposal: ownership boundary & order form clarifications
messages:
From: Eve Martin <eve.martin@galen.com>

Cc: contracts@galen.com, samir.patel@galen.com
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Galen - proposed MSA + order form redlines

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines Galen's legal team is proposing for the MSA and the updated order form. High level notes so you don't have to read both documents immediately:

- Section 5 (IP & Deliverables): Galen is asking for an explicit assignment of outputs generated by our services to Galen where the output is used directly in their product (they've proposed a limited assignment for "Productized Outputs").
- Training/Model Use: They want a right to opt-into retraining only with written approval; otherwise they request that Redwood not use customer data for model training.
- Feedback license: Galen proposes a reciprocal, nonexclusive license limited to internal improvement but also wants to prohibit sub-licensing for commercialization.
- Compliance evidence: procurement requested a list of audit artifacts and telemetry available for entitlement checks.

We know these items have broad implications across legal and commercial. Could you route to your legal and AM teams and propose a crisp counter (or fallback) we can discuss early next week?

Attaching: Galen_MSA_Redlines_20251202.docx (redline), OrderForm-v3-redlines.pdf

Best,

Subject: RE: Fwd: Galen - proposed MSA + order form redlines

Laura — read through their marked-up MSA. Short summary and suggested counter below. I kept it intentionally tight so we can push to commercial.

Summary of their ask:
- Assignment: full ownership of "Productized Outputs" (undefined; they left room for broad interpretation).
- Training: default prohibition on Redwood using Galen inputs to improve models unless prior written consent.
- Feedback: reciprocal license limited to "internal improvements" and no sublicensing for commercialization.

Risks/impact:
- Assignment for outputs opens us to losing re-use of model improvements derived from that customer's prompts (could impede our ability to offer shared models improvements).
- A blanket training prohibition constrains our continuous improvement and may increase unit cost.

Recommended counter (3-tier fallback):
1) Preferred (our ideal): license grant to Galen for Productized Outputs, perpetual, worldwide, exclusive only as to their product (narrowly defined), and expressly carve out Redwood's right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and non-identifiable learnings. Training: allow Redwood to use de-identified/aggregated usage for model improvement; if Galen wants an opt-out, make it a paid feature with a defined SLA for dedicated model instances. Feedback: provide a nonexclusive license back to Redwood limited to model improvement, with no downstream commercial sub-license (but permit internal tooling).
2) Middle (commercial compromise): allow Galen a time-limited exclusivity on Productized Outputs (e.g., 12 months) or a license with revenue-share triggers; training opt-out accepted but only for a subset of sensitive data classes (PII, PHI).
3) Walk: if they insist on assignment of all outputs and a blanket training ban without commercial cred (significant discount/commit), decline.

Draft language to propose (short):
- "Productized Outputs" means output that is incorporated, in whole or in material part, into Galen's public-facing product offerings as specifically identified in the Order Form. Redwood retains all underlying models, tooling, and rights to aggregated and de-identified telemetry.
- Training: "Customer Data shall not be used to train or fine-tune models for third-party customers except (i) in aggregated, de-identified form, or (ii) when Customer provides express written consent per Order Form. Dedicated training or model exclusivity is available as an add-on per mutually agreed SOW and fee schedule."
- Feedback: "Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, nonexclusive, royalty-free license to use Feedback for the sole purpose of improving Redwood’s services; such license does not permit Redwood to sublicense Customer proprietary code or to commercialize Customer-identifiable content."

I can draft a clean counter to send to Eve. Also see attached quick redline notes (I'll add inline comments in Drive).

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Galen - proposed MSA + order form redlines

Quick commercial read — happy to take on the negotiation with legal. A few notes on impact:

- If we move to a license-only model with a carve for "productized outputs" but no assignment, I expect Galen to push for a 10-15% discount and possibly a revenue share on productized features. We should budget for a single-digit price concession on committed TCV or an extended term (24 months) to avoid setting precedent.
- If they insist on assignment, we should only consider it for a tightly enumerated list of deliverables and tie it to a substantial uplift (25-40% discount plus indemnity protections).
- Training opt-out as a paid feature is clean and something we can operationalize (dedicated models / no telemetry). Expect an implementation lead time ~6–8 weeks and ongoing infra cost; recommend flagging as "Dedicated Model Plus" SKU.

For procurement asks (audit/evidence): we can provide an export of request logs, model version mapping, and token-level billing statements. Anything beyond that (full telemetry retention longer than standard) is billable as part of a compliance package.

I'll prepare two commercial positions — Standard (license, minimal concession) and Escalated (assignment limited + big uplift) — for Monday.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2025 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Galen - proposed MSA + order form redlines

Laura / team — operations readiness notes: 

- Evidence items: we can provide request logs (90 days default), model-version mapping per request, and tokenized billing exports. Extended retention or continuous audit exports will need 3rd-party storage and are chargeable.
- Training opt-out: we can implement a no-training flag at the tenant level. For full isolation and no telemetry collection we recommend a Dedicated deployment; engineering estimates 6 weeks to provision + 2 weeks for validation for the first environment.
- Productized output assignment: technically feasible to mark output as "exported product asset" in our pipeline but requires a delivery play to ensure provenance and escalation for misuse claims. This adds delivery effort ~2–3 weeks for integration per feature.

I'll collate the operational costs and a rough SOW. If legal wants a mechanism to list specific Productized Outputs, we should include a line in the Order Form that attaches an Exhibit listing those artifacts.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Galen - proposed MSA + order form redlines

Eve — thanks for the redlines and for the clear commentary. We reviewed internally. High-level position we can present to Galen next week:

1) Ownership: Redwood cannot accept broad assignment of all outputs. We will offer a narrow approach: (a) a license to use Productized Outputs (perpetual, worldwide) with an option to convert to time-limited exclusivity or assignment for specific, enumerated deliverables listed in Exhibit A of the Order Form for an additional fee.
2) Training: Redwood proposes that by default we may use aggregated and de-identified customer data for model improvements. If Galen wants an opt-out, we can offer a "no-training" paid option which will be implemented with tenant-level flags or a dedicated deployment (pricing TBD).
3) Feedback: Redwood needs a reciprocal license to use feedback for service improvement, limited to non-identifiable content and expressly excluding Customer proprietary code and IP for commercialization.

Next steps: Jordan will send a short counter-redline (language around Exhibit A and training opt-out), Ben will include the commercial tradeoffs (discount ranges / uplift for assignment), and Marissa will sketch an SOW for the dedicated/de-identified options. Can we schedule a 30-minute working call with Eve + Samir next Thursday 12/11?

Proposed times: 10:00am PT or 2:00pm PT. Please confirm when you have a moment.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales (West)
